title: Global Cross-Era Pilot v2: Coherence Constraint Violations (X–Y–Z)
description:
Overview
This project executes a global, cross-era pilot using the Coherence Constraint Instrument (X–Y–Z) to evaluate whether coherence violations systematically precede large-scale instability across civilizations, cultures, and historical periods.
The instrument evaluates coherence as a constraint satisfaction problem, defined strictly by consistency between:
X — declared commitments,
Y — observable actions,
Z — realized outcomes.
Only publicly documented evidence is used.
No intent inference, moral judgment, causal explanation, or outcome prediction is performed.
What This Project Does
Applies the same coherence rule across ancient, medieval, modern, and contemporary systems
Tests both collapsed and non-collapsed systems
Records whether, when, and how persistently coherence violations appear
Measures lead time between first violation and recognized instability
What This Project Does Not Do
Does not infer intent or motivation
Does not assign moral judgment
Does not predict future outcomes
Does not explain causes
It detects constraint violations only.
The Coherence Rule (X–Y–Z)
A system is coherent to the degree that its declared commitments (X), observable actions (Y), and realized outcomes (Z) remain mutually consistent over time.
A coherence violation is recorded when any of the following fail:
X ↔ Y
Y ↔ Z
X ↔ Z
Sample Frame
This pilot evaluates 20 system-era windows, including:
Historically Unstable Systems
Late Roman Republic
Western Roman Empire
Han Dynasty
Abbasid Caliphate
Byzantine Empire
Ming Dynasty
Qing Dynasty
Ottoman Empire
Spanish Empire
French Ancien Régime
Weimar Republic
USSR
Yugoslavia
Rwanda
Lebanon
Stability Controls
United Kingdom (post-1945)
Japan (post-1950)
Sweden (post-1950)
Canada (post-1950)
Singapore (post-1970)
Primary Outputs
For each system:
Presence or absence of coherence violations
Persistence of violations
Timing of first violation
Lead time to recognized instability (if applicable)
Falsification Conditions
This pilot fails if:
Collapsed systems show no prior coherence violations
Stable systems show persistent violations
Independent observers cannot replicate classifications
Violations occur only after instability begins
No post-hoc rule changes are allowed.
Status
This project is an instrument execution, not a theory proposal.
